clue.text: Second couple from Brazil rejected place to sleep?

parts.note: B is the second letter, as in a B grade or B-side

indicators.note: rejected means the pieces are turned back, so they are read backwards
from says the couple is taken from, and so placed after, the Brazilian city

parts.note: Rio is Brazil's best-known city, so Rio comes from Brazil
a duo is a couple, a pair

explanation.surface: A traveller turns down the second pair of rooms offered in Brazil as a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is B as in a B grade; the definition's question mark flags that a lady's private room is only loosely a place to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's private bedroom or dressing room, so a place where one might sleep; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Enhancements from competitor mistitled "petite"?

parts.note: and a contestant enhanced this way would be wrongly called petite

explanation.walkthrough: Look inside compeTITor, misTITled, peTITe: each has a TIT, crude slang for a breast, set into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery inserts that enlarge the bust, a kind of body enhancement.

clue.text: United's jet is fit for service

parts.note: U is a standard abbreviation for United, as in football club names
jet and sable are both words for black

explanation.surface: A football club's private plane has been passed as airworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' looks like an aircraft but is the colour: jet-black, sable in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be put to use is serviceable, ready to do its job.

clue.text: Partying with bar, nearly exposed

parts.note: partying is being out on a spree, out on a bender

indicators.note: nearly means the word loses its final letter, stopping just short

parts.note: the limbo is the dance done under a low bar

explanation.surface: Someone out at a party, propping up the bar, is close to being found out.
explanation.walkthrough: The limbo is a Caribbean party dance where you lean back to pass under a bar; 'nearly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a risky position with no support is an idiom for being vulnerable or exposed.

clue.text: Animal's hip described in Aristotle's letter

indicators.note: described in means drawn round, so the Greek letter encircles the other piece

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the one Aristotle wrote in
hip means fashionable, in

explanation.surface: An animal's hip joint is described in a letter written by Aristotle, the naturalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line around something.
explanation.definitionFit: A large thick-skinned horned mammal of Africa and Asia is one kind of animal.

clue.text: Thinks a little more, as on screen

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone ponders a bit longer, as characters do in films.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to think logically, so the verb forms match as synonyms.

clue.text: Check others shower on time

parts.note: the rest means the others
a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: Other people take a shower on schedule, a sort of inspection routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is a curb or restriction, the same sense as holding back.

clue.text: Queue heard following this lot to the highest point

definitions.text: Queue heard following this lot to the highest point

parts.words: Queue heard following this lot to the highest point
parts.note: queue is said like the letter Q, and this lot is the whole stretch of the alphabet that Q comes after, read as a phrase; that phrase also means on top

explanation.surface: A queue is heard following a group of people up to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: Q follows every letter from the first up to the one before it; name that stretch as 'first letter to sixteenth letter' and it is also a word meaning at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means on or at the top of something, at its very summit.

clue.text: Axes to split old plank, pretty ugly one

indicators.note: to split means the axes break into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: plank is slang for a stupid person
the x and y axes of a graph

explanation.surface: Someone takes axes to split an old plank, a very ugly job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty ugly' is itself the example: pretty and ugly contradict each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech joining contradictory terms; the phrase 'pretty ugly' is one such pairing.

clue.text: Hit double to knock out gutted team again

parts.note: to stun is to knock someone senseless

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are taken out, leaving only the outer letters of each word

explanation.surface: A boxer lands a hit, doubles up, and the team is gutted to be knocked out again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' here is a hit film; the double takes the actor's place in the dangerous scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who stands in for an actor in risky scenes of a hit film is a double.

clue.text: Performers no more precise

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what it was
an act is a performer or group of performers on a bill

explanation.surface: Performers who have retired are no more precise than they used to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and precise are synonyms, both meaning accurate in every detail.

clue.text: Split classic suit, is money OTT for tailoring?

indicators.note: tailoring is cutting and reshaping cloth, so these letters are cut and re-sewn into a new order

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, taken here as its letters

explanation.surface: A tailor asks whether paying so much for a classic suit is excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' is a break-up, not a seam: the answer is the classic line used when ending a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliché said by someone ending a relationship, so a classic line of a break-up.

clue.text: At sea, so plunders magnificent stuff

indicators.note: at sea means confused, all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, a pirate plunders treasures.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendours are grand, glorious things, magnificent possessions or sights.

clue.text: Perfectly brown bread, not sliced at first

indicators.note: not means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: toast is bread browned under heat

indicators.note: at first points to the first letter of the word sliced

explanation.surface: A baker's brown bread turns out perfectly, though it arrives unsliced.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom meaning exactly or just right, said of something that suits perfectly.

clue.text: Land expert on a rig most awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialist from dry land works clumsily on an oil rig.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies soil management and crop production is an expert on farmland.

clue.text: Sarong's packed by George!

parts.note: the packed contents of the word sarong are its inner letters ARON, which is the name Nora flipped round

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at how much a sarong has been stuffed with.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: flip NORA to get ARON, the letters packed inside S and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British exclamations of surprise or exasperation.

clue.text: When Charles should inherit, thug stands up as representative

parts.note: Charles would inherit after Elizabeth, ER, so post-ER

indicators.note: stands up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: yob is British slang for a lout or thug

explanation.surface: When the heir takes the throne, a thug stands up as a spokesman.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen; 'post-ER' is the time after her, when Charles inherits.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose image represents a cause or movement is its typical representative.

clue.text: See 1
Sex show about Liberals — it predicts the X-rating

indicators.note: about means the show goes around the other piece

parts.note: an expo is an exhibition, a show
it is a crossword term for sex appeal
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, so LL is Liberals

explanation.surface: A sex show featuring Liberal politicians is expected to get an adults-only rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X-rating' is the voter marking X on a ballot paper, not a film certificate.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey of voters leaving polling stations forecasts which boxes were marked with crosses.

clue.text: Making the most, saw savings — £100, current investment

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, a maxim
an ISA is a UK tax-free savings account

indicators.note: investment means clothing or enclosing, so the sum wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred pounds
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone making the most of their money saw savings of a hundred pounds on a current investment.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA (individual savings account) is a British tax-free savings scheme; 'investment' is used in its old sense of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something as great as possible is the act of increasing it to its fullest.

clue.text: Liking golf when retired causes annoyance

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a taste for something is a liking for it
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fondness for golf becomes irritating once the player has retired.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to nag or criticise, so it irritates or annoys someone.

clue.text: Train set ran mainly backwards

definitions.note: the main is the sea, so this is backwards at sea, toward a ship's stern

indicators.note: to train is to shape or school something, here working the letters into a new form

explanation.surface: A model train set ran mostly in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' looks like 'mostly' but means on the main, the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for toward or at the rear of a vessel, so backwards at sea.

clue.text: Gents' toilet playing romantic song

indicators.note: playing means fooling about, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe gives no letter

explanation.surface: A love song is being played in the men's lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: A Gents is a British name for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive 1973 Marvin Gaye soul hit, a classic love song.

clue.text: Senior group writes, taxing Americans I must infiltrate

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: must infiltrate means the piece gets inside the other piece

parts.note: the IRS is the US tax-collecting service
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old people's group writes letters complaining about Americans being taxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taxing' looks like an adjective, but the IRS (Internal Revenue Service) is the American body that taxes Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired people drawing a state allowance form a group of elderly citizens.

clue.text: Somewhat indigenous language

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the words that follow, a stretch of them

explanation.surface: A language that is partly native to a region.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: informal speech is a sort of homegrown local tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal vocabulary grows up within a group, a kind of home-made dialect of its own.

clue.text: Reportedly finish drawing tongue

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: to tie is to finish level, a drawn game

explanation.surface: An artist is said to complete a picture of a tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests art, but it means ending a match level.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language; this is the official language of Thailand.

clue.text: Fear of novelty mince pie on a hob

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up finely, so the letters are cut up and mixed

explanation.surface: Someone afraid of anything new distrusts a mince pie set on a cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince pie' looks like one item; 'mince' is the verb, chopping the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek roots mean dread of the new, an aversion to anything unfamiliar.

clue.text: See 10
Brief hippy movement's condition, close to assembly plant

indicators.note: brief means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: salsa is a Latin dance full of hip movement
if introduces a condition

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word

explanation.surface: A short-lived hippie movement's state of affairs, near an assembly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hippy' looks like the flower-power crowd, but it means a dance moving the hips.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant of the daisy family grown for its edible root, sometimes called oyster plant.
